title: Exponential graphs: the four basic shapes
question: Sketch the graph of $y = 3e^{2x}$, labelling any intercepts and the asymptote.

beats.say: First, the four basic shapes of exponential graphs. Most importantly, learn each shape, and which axis it is flipped in.
asks: Why learn the four shapes?

beats.say: Y equals E to the X: the basic shape. It grows faster and faster, and stays above the X axis.
asks: Why does it grow faster and faster?
Why is it always above the x-axis?

beats.say: Y equals E to the power minus X: a minus in front of X flips it in the Y axis.
asks: Why does a minus in front of x flip it in the y-axis?

beats.say: Y equals minus E to the X: a minus in front of the graph flips it in the X axis.
asks: Why does a minus in front flip it downwards?

beats.say: Y equals minus E to the power minus X: both minuses, so it is flipped twice, in both axes.
asks: How do I know which of the four shapes to use?

beats.say: Now sketch Y equals three E to the power two X. Start with empty axes at the side.
asks: Why start with empty axes?

beats.say: Four steps: first the shape, then the asymptote, then the intercepts, and last draw it.
asks: Why these four steps?
Why find the shape first?

beats.say: Step one, the shape. It is the minus sign that matters. Here there is no minus sign at all.
asks: Where would a minus sign be?

beats.say: So it has the shape of E to the X, from the corner. Lift it onto the axes.
asks: Why the shape of e to the x?

beats.say: The three and the two do not change the shape. They only stretch it, higher and steeper. Only a minus sign would flip it.
asks: What do the 3 and the 2 do then?

beats.say: Step two, the asymptote. As X goes left, E to the X gets closer and closer to the X axis, but never touches it.
asks: What is an asymptote?
Why does it never touch the x-axis?

beats.say: So the asymptote is Y equals zero, the X axis. Draw it as a dashed line.
asks: Why is the asymptote dashed?

beats.say: Three times a number close to zero is still close to zero. So our curve also hugs the X axis.
asks: Does the 3 move the asymptote?

beats.say: Step three, the intercepts. For the Y intercept, sub X equals zero.
asks: Why put x = 0 for the y-intercept?

beats.say: Y equals three E to the power two times zero.
asks: Why is it 2 times 0?

beats.say: Two times zero is zero, so we get three E to the power zero.
asks: Why is 2 times 0 zero?

beats.say: E to the power zero is one. So Y equals three times one, which is three.
asks: Why is e to the power 0 one?

beats.say: For the X intercept, sub Y equals zero. Three E to the power two X equals zero.
asks: Why put y = 0 for the x-intercept?

beats.say: Three times something is zero only if E to the power two X is zero. But a power of E is never zero.
asks: Why can we divide by 3?
Why is e to a power never zero?

do.text: e to any power is never zero

beats.say: So there are no solutions, and no X intercept. The curve never meets the X axis.
asks: Does no solutions mean I made a mistake?

read: A positive number to any power is still positive.
It can get very close to $0$, but never reach it.
**So $e^{2x} = 0$ has no solutions: the curve never meets the $x$-axis.**

beats.say: Step four, draw it. Stretch the shape through zero, three. It stays above the asymptote, and never cuts the X axis.
asks: Why is the curve steeper than e to the x?
